name: Protein crystals
headline: A different crystal suspension. A new formulation possibility.
body: Merck researchers crystallized pembrolizumab, an anticancer antibody, on the ISS. The published study reported a more homogeneous crystal-size distribution and lower suspension viscosity than the compared ground preparations.
evidence: Flight insights also informed improvements to Earth processing. This is evidence for valuable process development; it does not establish commercial orbital production or a clinical benefit.
application: Develop concentrated, manageable formulations of valuable biologics. The target is an agreed particle distribution and retained biological function.
bridge: A solution-growth cartridge could standardize liquid handling, temperature history, observation, recovery and batch records across successive research campaigns.
gate: Show the advantage survives an optimized Earth comparison, handling and functional testing. Protein integrity and pharmaceutical qualification remain specific to the product.
people: Merck is the demonstrated research participant. Future customer programs are proposed; no partnership is claimed.
plain: Proteins can form crystals. Their size and distribution affect how concentrated suspensions behave and flow.

name: Small-molecule crystals
headline: Orbit is already becoming a pharmaceutical process environment.
body: Varda’s ritonavir work demonstrated recovery of orbital-processed Form III; a 2026 paper examines its stability. Ritonavir is an antiviral and is separate from Merck’s antibody study.
evidence: On 20 October 2026, Varda announced W-7’s launch with a PROTAC cancer-drug crystallization experiment focused on solubility. The announcement establishes launched research, with performance results still to come.
application: Explore solid forms and processing routes for valuable drug candidates whose formulation is difficult.
bridge: Use a qualified thermal or solution recipe, sealed containment and a complete processing record. W-7’s mixing approach and a thermal crystallization route require different cartridge internals.
gate: Identify the returned form, stability, reproducibility and functional advantage. One successful compound does not validate every drug.
people: Varda is an existing operator and a potential competitor or ecosystem participant—not our customer.
plain: The same drug molecule can pack into different solid forms, changing properties such as stability and how it dissolves.

name: Cooling materials
short: The solid heart of a refrigerator
headline: Can an orbital process improve a material that moves heat?
body: NPG–camphor model alloys have been directionally solidified on the ISS. Separately, NPG has a strong pressure-driven caloric response on Earth. The flight study measured solidification, not refrigerator performance.
evidence: Research connects NPG microstructure with thermal hysteresis. Cycling can erase starting structures; useful heterogeneity can aid nucleation. Barocal is a real terrestrial company developing the broader barocaloric approach.
application: A durable solid-state cooling component for specialized thermal control, with household refrigeration as a longer-term ambition.
bridge: Test whether controlled solidification and phase distribution can create a persistent, useful nucleation structure. The flight mixture is not automatically the final refrigerant.
gate: Repeated-cycle thermal and pressure tests must show an advantage after preconditioning. Orbit-grown cooling improvement remains our hypothesis.
people: Barocal is an application-market example, not an orbital manufacturer or announced partner.
plain: Neopentyl glycol (NPG) is a research material that exchanges heat through pressure-driven phase changes. The aim is a solid working material for cooling.

name: MOF membranes
headline: A small selective layer could process a much larger stream.
body: Stanford and Berkeley are studying metal–organic framework growth in microgravity. Ground researchers have demonstrated oriented UiO-67 membranes with selective lithium transport.
evidence: BASF and Svante supply an industrial anchor: Earth-made MOF sorbents for carbon capture. Those sorbents are different from lithium membranes. Cemsica’s adjacent ISS membrane work used calcium-silicate, not MOFs.
application: A high-value, durable selective layer for lithium recovery or a precisely defined separation. Its value would accumulate over its service life.
bridge: Connect precursor dosing, growth on a substrate, defect inspection and post-return testing. Investigate whether orbital growth improves useful membrane performance.
gate: Beat optimized ground synthesis on selectivity, flux, adhesion, fouling and lifetime. Ground microfluidics already provides an important competing approach.
people: The organizations establish research and industrial relevance; none is represented as our customer.
plain: A metal–organic framework is a crystalline network with molecular-sized pores. Its chemistry and channel structure can enable selective separation.

name: Bijel reactor structures
short: Two intertwined networks. One tiny reactor.
org: NASA · UC IRVINE · PENN / ROWAN / POSTECH
headline: Build the internal plumbing of a chemical factory.
body: ACE-T5 investigated bicontinuous interfacially jammed emulsion gels: two continuous phases separated by a particle-stabilized interface. Ground researchers have used bijels for enzymatic reactive separation.
evidence: NASA’s investigation links structure, rheology and stability. This supports a manufacturing question; it does not establish a returned orbital reactor with better performance.
application: A small reusable reactor insert with connected flow paths and useful interfacial area for a specific chemical process.
bridge: Control mixing and thermal history, observe evolving geometry, and stabilize the network at the right moment.
gate: The structure must survive fixation and return, then improve transport, reaction performance and lifetime against an Earth-made core.
people: Named research groups are the evidence here. A commercial orbital bijel manufacturer was not verified.
plain: Two liquids form intertwined, continuous networks. Small particles help hold their shared boundary in place.

name: Photonic colloids
headline: An ordered three-dimensional structure, grown in orbit and returned.
body: ACE-T11 researchers reported large FCC colloidal crystals formed on the ISS and returned to Earth. The primary paper explicitly discusses optical-element applications.
evidence: The demonstrated result is the ordered colloidal structure. A stable, packaged chemical-sensing component is a proposed engineering extension.
application: A compact wavelength-selective element for environmental or industrial sensing.
bridge: Use controlled dispersion handling, thermal history, microscopy and an endpoint defined by structural order. Preserve that order through later processing.
gate: Demonstrate suitable optical contrast, low unwanted scattering, stability and integration after return.
people: Paper affiliations establish research participation, not commercial optical-device manufacturing.
plain: A regular three-dimensional array of small particles can shape how light travels. The structure itself becomes part of an optical component.
